¿DESEAS APRENDER A MIGRAR UN SITIO WEB DE WORDPRESS A OTRO DOMINIO O HOSTING?


Únete a nuestro curso para mostrarte cómo migrar un sitio web de WordPress completo a otro dominio o hosting, para dicho proceso, podemos utilizar uno de estos dos plugins: All in One WP Migration o SiteGround Migrator.


All in One WP Migration es un plugin que facilita la migración de un sitio hecho en WordPress de forma rápida y sencilla.


Permite exportar todo el contenido como entradas, post, plugins, base de datos, imágenes, temas, etc.


Para realizar este proceso no necesitas ningún tipo de conocimiento técnico ni de programación, ya que se realiza de una forma fácil y veloz.


Para migrar un sitio web en WordPress con el plugin All in One WP Migration, básicamente hay que realizar los siguientes pasos:

  • Instalar el plugin All-in-One WP Migration.

  • Dar clic al botón de exportar para compilar tu base de datos, archivos de medios, plugins, y temas en un archivo compacto.

  • Desempacar el archivo en la nueva ubicación o dominio con una función de “arrastrar y soltar” fácil de usar en el panel de WordPress de tu nuevo sitio web.


SiteGround Migrator es un plugin gratuito de WordPress desarrollado por SiteGround que nos ayuda a migrar un sitio web con WordPress a tu cuenta en SiteGround desde cualquier otra compañía de alojamiento web.


Para migrar un sitio web en WordPress con el plugin SiteGround Migrator, básicamente hay que realizar los siguientes pasos:

  • Generar un token de migración en el Site Tools de SiteGround.

  • Instalar el plugin SiteGround Migrator en tu WordPress.

  • Pegar el token de migración en el plugin para comenzar la migración.

  • Comprobar tu sitio y actualizar los registros DNS para terminar la migración.

DISTRIBUTION

Distribution was created for transfer primary costs from a sender cost center to receiving controlling objects. During distribution, only cost centers or business process can be used as sender.

A distribution receiver can be a cost center, WBS element, internal order, cost object, or a business process. You can restrict the number of receiver categories in customizing.

Primary Postings (such as, energy costs) are collected on a cost center, and allocated at the end of the period by means of the user-defined key.

You can only distribute primary costs. During this process, the original cost element remains the same. Line items are posted for the sender as well as for the receiver, enabling the allocation to be recorded exactly.

You can reverse distributions as often as required. You use the Cycle-Segment method to define sender-receiver relationships.


ASSESSMENT

Assessment was created to transfer primary and secondary costs from a sender cost center to receiving controlling objects. During assessment, cost center or business processes can be used as senders.

The receivers for an assessment can be a cost center, WBS element, internal order, cost object, or a business process. You can restrict the number of receiver categories in customizing.

Primary and secondary posting are allocated at the end of the period by the user-defined key.

During assessment, the original cost elements are summarized into assessment cost elements (secondary cost element category = 42). As the system writes fewer total records, the assessment has a better performance than periodic reposting and distribution.

The system does not display the original cost elements in the receivers. Therefore, assessment is useful if the cost drilldown for the receiver is not important.

Similar to distribution, the partner is updated in the totals record during distribution. You can reverse assessments as often as required. You use the Cycle-Segment method to define sender-receiver relationships.

Becoming a chartered surveyor (MRICS) is one of the most valuable career moves in construction and property — higher earning potential, international recognition, and a designation clients and employers trust. And yet the APC (Assessment of Professional Competence) is where capable professionals with strong careers get referred every single assessment window. Not because they lack experience — but because nobody taught them how the assessment actually works: how assessors read a Summary of Experience, what the panel prepares before your interview, or why "applying too early" is officially the most common reason candidates fail.


This course fixes that. Every lesson is built directly from the official RICS documents — the APC Candidate Guide, the pathway guides, the Rules of Conduct, the Ethics Decision Tree, and crucially the Assessor Guide, Chairperson Guide and Competency Questioning Matrix that your panel itself follows. You will prepare against the same standards your assessors apply, because you will have read their instructions too.


════════════════════════════════


THE COMPLETE SYSTEM — 9 SECTIONS, 52 LESSONS


SECTION 1 — MRICS OVERVIEW & ROUTE SELECTION (6 lessons)

What MRICS is and why it matters; the five assessment routes explained; eligibility rules and a decision matrix that picks your route from your actual qualifications and experience; the APC lifecycle from enrolment to result; how the counsellor relationship works; and your personal candidacy calendar with every milestone dated.


SECTION 2 — THE COMPETENCY FRAMEWORK (6 lessons)

The mandatory and technical competencies decoded; what Levels 1, 2 and 3 really mean (knowledge, application, reasoned advice); how to read your pathway guide; selecting your competency set strategically — including which optional competencies to declare and which to avoid; mapping your career onto the framework with a competency matrix; and running an honest gap analysis that becomes a dated development plan.


SECTION 3 — ASSESSMENT PLATFORM & ADMINISTRATION (6 lessons)

The candidate platform mastered: the diary and logbook kept the way assessors read them; the CPD record structured correctly from day one; version control so you always know which document is current; the consistency sweep that catches contradictions between your documents before assessors do; and the readiness map that tracks every administrative requirement.


SECTION 4 — WRITING THE SUMMARY OF EXPERIENCE (6 lessons)

The statement anatomy for each level, with the official per-level briefs; writing personal evidence with "I" verbs and real particulars instead of team narratives; the four-move method for Level 3 reasoned advice (situation, options with criteria, recommendation with reasoning, outcome); allocating the official word limits — 1,500 across all mandatory competencies, 4,000 across all technical — with a worked allocation; a full rewrite workshop with before/after examples of weak and strong statements; and the compliance audit before you freeze.


SECTION 5 — BUILDING A HIGH-QUALITY CASE STUDY (6 lessons)

Choosing the right project with a weighted scorecard; the 24-month window rule and how to verify it; selecting issues that carry genuine options and advice; writing reasoned advice with the because-clause intact; the critical appraisal that referral reports most often flag as missing; the four-section structure with word budgets (~500/1,150/850/450 within the 3,000 limit); the confidentiality statement done properly — consent or disguise, never half of each; and the quality gate plus question harvest that turns your report into interview preparation.


SECTION 6 — ETHICS, RULES OF CONDUCT & PROFESSIONALISM (6 lessons)

The five Rules of Conduct verbatim with their official example behaviours and the six principles beneath them; the RICS Ethics Decision Tree walked node by node — including the official "unsure: do not proceed" instruction; conflicts of interest and the identify-assess-disclose-manage playbook; gifts, hospitality, bribery awareness and money-laundering red flags; PII, complaints and acting within competence; and ten drilled ethics scenarios with model reasoning — your preparation for the Professionalism Module, your Ethics statement, and the chairperson's closing questions, all at once.


SECTION 7 — CPD & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT (5 lessons)

The official definition and three principles; 48 hours per 12 months with at least 50% formal, including the timing rule most preliminary-review candidates miss; planning your CPD year from your actual competency gaps; writing learning outcomes that answer interview questions by themselves; linking CPD to competencies the way assessors cross-reference it; and the five-check audit before any submission.


SECTION 8 — THE FINAL ASSESSMENT INTERVIEW (6 lessons)

The hour's structure stage by stage, and every panel role decoded — including the silent auditor; the ten-minute presentation built to a timed arc, with the assessor guide's own instruction to weight it heavily; the Competency Questioning Matrix decoded — how your questions are prepared from your own documents before you join the call, and how to predict 70-80% of them; answer architectures for each level so you never answer a Level 3 question with a Level 2 story; recovering from blanks, errors and hard moments professionally; and the three-mock rehearsal programme with self-marking sheets, an interview-week schedule and a day protocol.


SECTION 9 — REFERRAL, RESILIENCE & FINAL READINESS (5 lessons)

The preliminary review decoded — three-document feedback, Ready/Not Ready, and why silence in the report is a pass; understanding referral: the report's official standard (every deficiency tied to a competency, every deficiency with a stated remedy) and the five-step decode method; running a resubmission as a targeted campaign, not a repeat; and the five-panel readiness gate — the evidence-based go/no-go that stops you applying too early, which the counsellor guide names as the most common referral cause of all.
